summary: Addendum to the same-day cowork-detect-loop-flow-review brief: user is going on ~1 week vacation, the entire fleet runs on the user's personal PC (no cloud hosting), and the machine will sleep and/or fully shut down for that span -- a duration exceeding the 2 already-confirmed sleep-outages (2.5d, 4d) that self-healed cleanly, and possibly involving a full CronCreate-session-ending shutdown rather than sleep, which is untested. New §D added to the brief (docs/architecture-briefs/2026-08-22-cowork-detect-loop-flow-review.md, not the .vi.md sibling) with 4 new CONFIRMED findings (F9-F12) plus a pre/post-vacation checklist. TWO of those findings are genuine gaps worth a follow-up cycle, not just live-state observations: (F10, NEW, not previously surfaced) scripts/agents-flow/cowork-catchup-predicate.js -- the designed guaranteed-slot catch-up mechanism from docs/architecture-briefs/2026-07-22-cowork-guaranteed-slot-catchup-design.md -- is a real built module and IS wired into cowork-match-slots.js's own JSON output (catchup_raw[]), but grep-confirmed ZERO references to catchup/catchup_raw exist in any of the 3 documented consumer sites: docs/agents/cowork-team/flow/main.md (the design's own Step 4.55 sub-flow catchup-check.md was never created -- file does not exist), scripts/agents-flow/cowork-tick-preflight.sh (Step 6.5 never added), and scripts/agents-flow/cowork-guaranteed-slot-firer.sh (the launchd backstop -- still reads only .slots[] filtered to guaranteed==true, never .catchup_raw[], despite the original design brief's own §2.3 explicitly calling this exact plane 'the plane most likely to actually deliver the catch-up during a session-down window'). Consequence: the plain slot-match window is +/-2 minutes around the cron's exact scheduled UTC minute; any guaranteed dish/post (chef morning/EOD/evening, digest-daily/sunday, tnb-audit, fb-daily/weekend) whose exact minute falls during any host-down window -- including possibly the very day the user returns from vacation, since manually re-arming is an unscheduled human action with no guarantee of landing within that +/-2min window -- is silently and permanently skipped, with no late-fire, no structured miss record (that logic was part of the same never-wired design), and no dedicated alert. No duplicate-publish risk exists either way (a separate, working mechanism -- the published-marker gate documented in the brief's §B -- independently prevents that), so this is a coverage/silent-loss gap, not a correctness-of-what-does-fire gap. (F12, NEW) There is no SessionStart hook or any other automated 'long gap since last activity -> re-arm the 3 cron skills' mechanism anywhere in .claude/settings.json or .claude/settings.local.json -- confirmed by direct read, only PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop/SubagentStart hooks exist, none reference cron-cowork-team/cron-detect-loop/cron-standalone-team at all. Re-arming after a full shutdown is a prose instruction in the project's own CLAUDE.md ('re-arm ... after every session restart'), not a code-enforced hook -- 100% dependent on the router or user remembering. If the first post-vacation session gets compacted, interrupted, or is opened for an unrelated quick question before the router's CLAUDE.md preamble runs, the entire fleet (including system-auditor, the one component that would normally notice and alert on prolonged silence) stays dark indefinitely with zero self-alerting fallback. Nothing was fixed -- this is observe-and-report only, per the same dispatch-table scope as the original brief.
_note_to_agent_father: Two follow-up candidates surfaced, neither implemented here (scope = observation only): (1) F10 -- either finish wiring the already-built scripts/agents-flow/cowork-catchup-predicate.js into its 3 originally-designed consumer sites (docs/architecture-briefs/2026-07-22-cowork-guaranteed-slot-catchup-design.md §2.3 has the exact call-site plan, including the launchd firer path specifically), OR make an explicit PO-ratified decision that guaranteed-slot catch-up is intentionally out of scope going forward and retire/archive the half-built predicate module + its dead cowork-schedule.json._dish_type_catchup_config rather than leaving it silently inert. Either resolution is acceptable; leaving it half-wired with no one aware is not. (2) F12 -- consider a lightweight SessionStart hook (or a router-side CLAUDE.md-adjacent check) that measures elapsed time since the last successful cron tick (e.g. via docs/data/dev-team-idle-widen-state.json.updated_at or the cron-registration:* task_claim heartbeat_at fields) and either auto-invokes the 3 re-arm skills or at minimum sends a loud one-time WORK/bug telegram flagging 'fleet has been dark for Nh, re-arm may be needed' -- this is exactly the class of gap a purely-manual convention leaves open, and system-auditor itself can't help since it would be dark too. Both are P2/backlog-appropriate, not urgent -- route to PO for prioritization, not an emergency dispatch. This signal and the original 2026-08-22-cowork-detect-loop-flow-review.json signal (already drained/processed) both point at the same brief file, now with an added §D.
